title: Cannot differentiate between explicit void return and optional return in method metadata
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in Godot 4.5.2, 4.6, 4.7


### System information

Godot v4.7.dev3 - macOS Tahoe (26.3.1) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Metal (Forward+) - integrated Apple M1 Pro (Apple7) - Apple M1 Pro (10 threads) - 16.00 GiB memory

### Issue description

Due to the changes in return type checks in inherited classes, there is a need to differentiate between a method that has an explicit retun type of `void` and one that is optional.

The following code is valid:
```gdscript
class Base:
    func foo():
        pass

    func bar() -> void:
        pass


class ExtendsBase:
    extends Base
    func foo():
        return 'bar'
```

However, when looking at the metadata, `Base.foo` appears to have a `void` return type in the metadata.  The metadata is the same as the `bar` method that has an explicit `void` return type.  Since the parser will not allow you to include a return clause with a value in a `void` return type function, I cannot generate a dynamic wrapper for `foo` that would return a value (even though, in this example it would be valid).

I feel like many people create method stubs using `pass` for methods that should/could return values when implemented in sub classes.  Being able to tell the difference between optional/inferred and explicit `void` return types makes generating wrapper code easier and more reliable.

Example meta data of inferred `void`
```
{
  "args": [],
  "default_args": [],
  "flags": 1,
  "id": 0,
  "name": "foo",
  "return": {
    "class_name": "",
    "hint": 0,
    "hint_string": "",
    "name": "",
    "type": 0,
    "usage": 6
  }
}
```

Example metadata of explicit `void`
```
{
  "args": [],
  "default_args": [],
  "flags": 1,
  "id": 0,
  "name": "bar",
  "return": {
    "class_name": "",
    "hint": 0,
    "hint_string": "",
    "name": "",
    "type": 0,
    "usage": 6
  }
}
```


## Workarounds


### Replace `pass` with `return`
The user can replace `pass` with `return` in all methods they expect to return a value.  This will make the return value optional and the method will now have a `Variant` return type in the metadata.  This should be the solution going forward, but isn't great for the transition period between 4.6 and 4.7.


### Add a way to allow the user to deal with this.
On my side, I can add functionality that user can use to override the return type when generating dynamic wrappers.  This has some restrictions on timing and usage.


## Possible Implementations
* Add a new `MethodFlag` to indicate that the method does not have a declared return type (used with `flags` in the metadata).  This seems to make the most sense.
* Add a `PropertyUsageFlag` for `return.usage` to indicate the return value is optional.  This doesn't seem to fit the kinds of values in `PropertyUsageFlag`, but it would work.
* Add another field to the metadata.  This does not feel like a good idea.

### Steps to reproduce

```gdscript
extends SceneTree
class Base:
	func foo():
		pass

	func bar() -> void:
		pass


func _init() -> void:
	for method in (Base as Variant).get_script_method_list():
		print(JSON.stringify(method, "    "))
```
Run the following standalone script.  The metadata for both functions is the same except for the name.  There is no way to tell which has an explicit void and which is inferred.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

See steps to reproduce

### Edit 
updated tested versions.  This appears to be how the metadata has always been, but it has become an issue in 4.7 due to the additional return type checking that was added.
